scope: The original 200 onomatopoeia cards and the subsequent ぶかぶか addition: 201 word catalogs, using their reviewed taught senses rather than every dictionary sub-sense.

additional_lexical_sources.review: Direct author review of the actual dictionary entries and the complete new card. The examples and English explanations are original. Clothing and footwear fit is the taught focus; material deformation and instrument sound remain dictionary side notes. Both scripts share one identity, no JLPT level is inferred, and ぶくぶく is excluded for overlap. No independent or native-speaker review is claimed.

model_evidence: Observed existing Azure deployment metadata before generation; deployment and capacity were not changed.
shared_style: Clean modern editorial illustration with soft natural colours, gentle shading and clear shapes, like a picture in a Japanese children's magazine or recipe book. One clear subject, uncluttered background, square composition. Absolutely no text, no letters, no kana, no kanji, no numbers, no speech bubbles, no sound-effect lettering, no watermark, no signature. Original artwork, not imitating any specific artist or work.
advisory_method: Every new output inspected directly or in a contact sheet; unclear cases enlarged. Actual observations are hash-pinned and eligibility is explicit.
owner_review: Prior 120-image batch acceptance is preserved. Explicit later approvals are recorded per scene; no unrecorded owner approval is inferred.
limits: Still images associate with taught uses; they do not prove sound, taste, temperature, private feelings or preceding events.
Current symmetric word exclusions remain in force; no claim of exhaustive visual uniqueness across every future card is made.
Advisory review is not independent two-model agreement, native-speaker certification or a measured false-approval/false-rejection rate.
Promotions of provisional article-only holds are documented in the actual observations; they are not owner-labeled review errors.
Original PNGs and request receipts are retained locally outside the runtime payload; prompts are reproducible but generation is not deterministic.
generation_invocations records outer generation attempts, not every internal rate-limit retry or a verified billing count.
Physical-phone behavior and learning effectiveness are not certified by this visual review.

scenes.description: A mechanical mantel clock has twelve clear hour markers and two hands, with exposed side gears and small ticking marks beside the escapement.
scenes.basis: Meaning and 時計がかちかちと音を立てている teach clock-like clicking.
scenes.generation_scene: Close view of one small mechanical mantel clock on a wooden shelf in soft daylight. The round ivory dial is NOT blank: it has exactly twelve distinct dark radial hour baton markers, evenly spaced around the whole circumference. The four cardinal markers are slightly longer. All twelve are simple solid straight strokes, without numerals or lettering. Two clearly distinct clock hands pivot from the center and point to the hour markers. A brass case has an open side exposing a small toothed gear and its contacting escapement. Two short subtle vibration strokes immediately beside the escapement suggest repeated little hard ticking sounds, not a loud bell. Show the entire circular marked dial clearly from a nearly frontal angle, with the side mechanism also visible. Mechanically plausible illustration, no exaggerated gear precision claim. No blank face, alarm bells, digital screen, brand name, numbers, Roman numerals, letters, text, sound-effect words or speech bubbles.

advisory_review.note: Full-size inspection confirms twelve distinct radial hour markers around the dial, two hands and an exposed side mechanism with local ticking strokes. The face is no longer blank; plain baton markers keep the picture free of numerals and lettering. The small-hard-click association is preserved without claiming audible evidence or precise clock engineering.
